description: Reusable proof prerequisites for proof-carrying Type-4 frontier packets. Target packets cite these fact_id values; packet-local models may add only packet-specific current status.

evidence_requirement_vocabulary.focused-executable: A focused positive or hard-negative expectation must exercise the fact boundary.
evidence_requirement_vocabulary.formal-or-mechanized: A formal proof, proof obligation, or machine-checked model must justify the rewrite precondition.
evidence_requirement_vocabulary.source-evidence: The source program must expose evidence for the fact; names alone are not enough.

accepted_evidence: ordered integer literal bounds
asserted Guard(BoundOrder) evidence on a dominating exiting inverse guard, for example if hi < lo then raise/return/throw before the clamp
asserted Guard(BoundOrder) evidence on a positive branch guard, for example if lo <= hi then evaluate the clamp and the other branch exits
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a real clamp pair by itself; the paired members must also satisfy numeric-clamp.integer-domain.
implementation_guidance: Represent only dominating exiting inverse guards and positive branch guards as bound-order evidence.
Reject parameter naming, non-exiting checks, swapped bounds, and wrong min/max nesting.
rejected_evidence: parameter names such as lower/upper or minimum/maximum
non-exiting guard expressions
swapped bounds or wrong min/max nesting
facts.summary: The lower bound must be proven <= the upper bound before min(max(x, lo), hi), max(min(x, hi), lo), ternary clamp, and library clamp forms can share a Clamp value.
facts.title: Clamp bound order

accepted_evidence: integer literals
asserted integer parameter/domain evidence on each clamp operand
language/type evidence that excludes float, NaN, and non-total-order behavior
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a real clamp pair by itself; the paired members must also satisfy numeric-clamp.bound-order.
implementation_guidance: Gate clamp canonicalization to integer-domain operands.
Keep language domains that can include floats or NaN outside exact clamp admission.
rejected_evidence: Python dynamic numeric parameters without integer-domain evidence
TypeScript/JavaScript number domains
Go cmp.Ordered or other generic ordered domains that can include floats
facts.summary: Clamp canonicalization is restricted to integer-domain operands so float/NaN-sensitive min/max and comparison-chain forms stay closed.
facts.title: Clamp integer domain

accepted_evidence: focused executable positives where sum, reduce, or fold surfaces converge inside the detector's controlled aggregate value model
source or fixture evidence that the compared members use the same aggregate value coordinate and additive contribution
focused hard negatives where product/count, wrong-seed, float-sensitive, overflow-sensitive, or unproven numeric-domain variants remain split
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit aggregate convergence by itself; source identity, identity/empty behavior, step coordinate, and effect facts remain separate.
implementation_guidance: Use this fact only for the controlled reduction slice where the detector value model has already proven the same additive aggregate coordinate.

Do not treat this fact as a runtime no-overflow integer proof; fixed-width overflow, C/C++ undefined behavior, floating-point, NaN, signed-zero-sensitive, string-concatenating, or overloaded arithmetic still need separate proof facts.
Attach new language surfaces by emitting domain evidence, not by broadening reducer spelling matches.
rejected_evidence: using focused Python, JavaScript, Ruby, or TypeScript aggregate fixtures as proof that all runtime values are finite integers
TypeScript number, Java double, Go float64, Rust f64, Swift Double, or C floating-point aggregate domains
C/C++ signed overflow or undefined behavior used as cross-language aggregate evidence without a no-overflow proof
fixed-width overflow-sensitive integer reductions compared across languages without an overflow-domain proof
dynamic arithmetic where operands may be strings, floats, or overloaded values outside the controlled fixture's value model
facts.summary: Reduction arithmetic may enter the controlled aggregate slice only under the detector's focused aggregate value model; this is not a runtime finite-integer/no-overflow proof, and float, NaN, signed-zero, overflow, and dynamic numeric behavior remain outside the fact.
facts.title: Aggregate value-model numeric domain

accepted_evidence: focused executable positives where seeded min/max selection folds preserve the same comparator direction, explicit seed, and selected value coordinate
source or fixture evidence that the compared members stay inside the detector's controlled selection value-order model
focused hard negatives where min-vs-max direction, unseeded defaults, NaN-sensitive, custom-comparator, or unproven numeric-order variants remain split
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit min/max or relational selection convergence by itself; source identity, seed/identity behavior, comparator coordinate, and effect facts remain separate.
implementation_guidance: Use this fact only for controlled seeded selection where comparator direction, explicit seed, and selected value coordinate are all proven.
Do not treat this fact as a runtime strict-total-order proof for arbitrary untyped or generic ordered values.

Reject NaN-sensitive float domains, custom comparison protocols, generic ordered type parameters that can include floats, and untyped relational comparisons outside the controlled selection fixture model.
Keep comparator direction and seed/domain facts separate so min-vs-max and seeded-vs-unseeded boundaries remain visible.
rejected_evidence: JavaScript or Python relational comparisons over untyped values used as a broad runtime total-order proof
TypeScript number, Swift Double, Java double, Go float64, Rust f64, or C floating-point min/max surfaces without explicit NaN handling
generic ordered constraints such as Go cmp.Ordered when the instantiation can include floating-point values
custom comparator or overloaded comparison methods without API identity and purity proof
facts.summary: Seeded min/max and relational selection may enter the controlled selection slice only when the detector proves the same seed, comparator direction, and selected value-order coordinate; broad runtime total-order, NaN-sensitive, and custom-order surfaces stay outside exact admission.
facts.title: Selection value-order numeric domain

accepted_evidence: focused hard negatives where NaN-sensitive min/max, comparison, or clamp forms remain split
focused hard negatives where signed-zero-sensitive abs or conditional-negate forms remain split
source/type evidence showing a surface is floating-point or otherwise can observe NaN, signed zero, or non-associative arithmetic

implementation_guidance: Record NaN, signed-zero, and non-associative float behavior as explicit hard-negative evidence instead of burying it in prose caveats.
Do not reuse integer-domain or total-order facts for floating-point APIs unless a future proof explicitly models NaN and signed-zero behavior.
Keep identical float groupings eligible to converge only when the grouping and API semantics are unchanged.
rejected_evidence: assuming Math.min/min/max or comparison-chain behavior agrees in the presence of NaN
assuming abs(x) equals x >= 0 ? x : -x for signed-zero-sensitive domains
reassociating or regrouping floating-point addition/multiplication as if it were an associative integer operation

facts.title: Floating-point special-value boundary

accepted_evidence: comparison predicates whose results are booleans
the same element variable and the same literal/value coordinates on both sides
a boolean context where operand values are not observed
language or source evidence that excludes overloaded, value-returning, or effectful boolean operands
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a quantifier/loop convergence by itself; source identity, purity, counterexample-loop, and vacuous-truth facts are separate requirements.
implementation_guidance: Normalize De Morgan only when operands are proven boolean values.
Reject value-returning boolean contexts, overloaded comparison semantics, and predicate calls unless separate effect/purity evidence exists.
Attach new language surfaces by emitting boolean-operand evidence, not by adding language-specific detector branches.
rejected_evidence: value-returning and/or operands whose value, not only truthiness, is observed
overloaded comparison or predicate calls with effects
changed predicates such as x != 0 or x != 1
facts.summary: A De Morgan rewrite may be used only when both sides operate on proven boolean operands, not on language-specific value-returning boolean expressions.
facts.title: De Morgan over proven boolean operands

accepted_evidence: a universal quantifier/all/every surface over a single element predicate
an explicit loop whose only counterexample branch returns literal false
matching predicate coordinates between the quantifier and the loop counterexample
short-circuit order that stops at the first counterexample
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a loop/quantifier convergence by itself; vacuous truth, source identity, predicate purity, and any boolean rewrite facts remain separate.
implementation_guidance: Model only loops where the counterexample branch is the sole early false exit.
Keep extra loop control, observed loop effects, and unsupported body shapes closed until separate evidence exists.
Pair this fact with quantifier.vacuous-truth before admitting an all/every-style surface.
rejected_evidence: counterexample branches that return non-false payloads
loop bodies with extra observed effects, break, continue, else effects, or unsupported control
predicate-coordinate changes between the quantifier and the loop
facts.summary: A universal quantifier can match an early-return loop only when the loop is a pure counterexample scan that returns false at the first not-P element.
facts.title: Universal quantifier as counterexample loop

accepted_evidence: the quantifier surface returns true for an empty input
the explicit loop falls through to literal true after exhausting the same input
no loop else block, final payload, or post-loop effect changes the empty-input result
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a quantifier/loop convergence by itself; it only closes the empty-input boundary for a separately proven counterexample loop.
implementation_guidance: Treat empty-input behavior as a first-class proof fact, not as a side effect of loop-shape matching.
Keep loops that return false or a payload after exhaustion outside all/every admission.
Require this fact whenever a universal quantifier surface is matched to an explicit loop.
rejected_evidence: fallthrough returns false or a non-boolean payload
post-loop code changes the empty-input result
collection APIs with non-vacuous empty behavior
facts.summary: Universal quantifier rewrites must preserve the empty-input result: no counterexamples means true.
facts.title: Universal quantifier vacuous truth

accepted_evidence: the quantifier and explicit loop consume the same local iterable binding or receiver place
no reassignment or mutation changes the source between the two forms
the quantifier element and loop element refer to the same traversal coordinate
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a quantifier/loop convergence by itself; it only rules out different receivers, iterators, or traversal sources.
implementation_guidance: Require same-source provenance for the quantifier and loop traversal.
Reject different iterable bindings, mutated receivers, and derived iterables whose order/cardinality relation is not proven.
Let each frontend emit receiver/place evidence for its language surface.
rejected_evidence: different iterable bindings or receiver places
receiver or iterator mutation during traversal
derived iterables whose cardinality/order relationship is not proven
facts.summary: The quantifier and explicit loop must traverse the same source in the same order before their predicates can be compared.
facts.title: Iteration same-source identity

accepted_evidence: local comparisons over the loop or quantifier element and literals
no calls, assignments, yields, awaits, mutations, or logging inside the predicate or loop body
no observed state before the early return or inside the quantifier predicate
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a quantifier/loop convergence by itself; it only permits comparing short-circuit boundaries after predicate effects are closed.
implementation_guidance: Treat helper calls, mutation, logging, yield, await, and assignment as closed unless separate purity/effect evidence exists.
Keep short-circuit timing as behavior-defining when side effects can be observed.
Attach language surfaces through effect evidence producers or admitted purity resolvers.
rejected_evidence: predicate helper calls unless callee purity is proven
observed counters or logging before return
iterator, receiver, or captured-state mutation during traversal
facts.summary: The predicate must be pure enough that quantifier and loop short-circuiting observe the same effects and stop at the same first counterexample.
facts.title: Pure predicate/effect safety

accepted_evidence: callback bodies made only of local value construction, comparisons, field reads, and pure arithmetic over the current element
no logging, mutation, assignment, yield, await, throw, or helper call with unknown effects inside the callback
focused hard negatives that keep observed callback effects behavior-defining
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit HoF convergence by itself; receiver/source identity, callback meaning, and output-channel facts remain separate requirements.
implementation_guidance: Use this for map/filter/filter_map/flat_map callbacks, not just boolean predicates.
Treat helper calls, mutation, logging, yield, await, throw, and assignment as closed without separate effect evidence.
Keep evaluation timing and observed callback effects out of value-only HoF facts.
rejected_evidence: callbacks that print, log, mutate, assign, yield, await, throw, or call unproven helpers
callbacks whose laziness or evaluation timing is observable
receiver or captured-state mutation during callback execution
facts.summary: Higher-order callback rewrites may compare value outputs only after callback effects and evaluation timing are proven unobservable for the admitted surface.
facts.title: Pure callback/effect safety

accepted_evidence: filter_map, compactMap, or equivalent callback forms whose absence branch drops exactly the same elements as the explicit filter predicate
guarded builders that push only on the same drop-condition complement
match, if-let, and and_then-style option forms that expose the same absence condition

implementation_guidance: Treat the drop condition as a first-class coordinate distinct from the emitted value expression.
Reject changed predicates, inverted predicates, extra filters, and post-filter drops unless a separate proof connects them.
Keep explicit filter+map chains and option-producing callbacks connected through this fact, not through API spelling.
rejected_evidence: same emitted value with a changed filter/drop predicate
extra post-filter conditions that can remove emitted values
truthiness checks that decide dropping from the emitted payload instead of the option channel
facts.summary: Filter-map convergence requires proof that both surfaces drop exactly the same source elements before emitted values are compared.
facts.title: Filter-map drop-condition coordinate

accepted_evidence: the Some/Just/present branch emits the same value coordinate as the explicit map expression
guarded builders push the same value expression as the option-producing callback emits
literal, parameter, field, or arithmetic coordinates are preserved through lowering
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit filter-map convergence by itself; drop condition, source identity, option channel, and callback purity facts remain separate.
implementation_guidance: Compare emitted values independently from the condition that decides whether a value is emitted.
Reject Some/Just payload changes, derived payloads, and wrong pushed values unless a separate value proof connects them.
Keep wrapped absence payloads as emitted values when the option channel says they are present.
rejected_evidence: same drop condition with a changed emitted value
mapping Option/Maybe values as payloads instead of emitting their inner present values
derived emitted values without a value-equivalence proof
facts.summary: Filter-map convergence requires the present branch, explicit map expression, or guarded push to emit the same value coordinate.
facts.title: Filter-map emitted value coordinate

falsey payloads such as 0, false, or empty strings that remain emitted when wrapped as present values
wrapped absence payloads such as Some(None) that remain present values in nested option domains

nullish/defaulting idioms that erase present null payload distinctions

same variable names across files without binding, parameter-role, or source evidence

status_vocabulary.admitted-real-pair: The fact is reusable and has current real-pair evidence, but detector admission still depends on every fact required by the packet.
status_vocabulary.modeled-controlled: The fact is implemented or machine-checked for controlled evidence; individual real-corpus members still need source evidence.
status_vocabulary.retired: The fact id is retained only for historical artifacts and should not be cited by new packets.
status_vocabulary.specified-not-modeled: The fact is specified as a reusable prerequisite, but no detector/proof implementation can consume it yet.
